subject: Caldera Health — capacity hedge analysis: private vs reserved GPU paths
body:
From: Susan Park <susan@calderahealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Caldera Health Procurement <procurement@calderahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFP: inference hosting for regulated patient workflows

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking a look at our RFP. We are evaluating two hosting postures for our new patient-facing triage product that will run in the US: a private VPC/on-prem control plane (air-gapped option possible) vs. reserved dedicated capacity in a tenant-isolated pool. High level:

- Expected steady-state: ~35 QPS of short text generation (avg 150 tokens) for NLU and assisted-summary flows.
- Peak patterns: daily 3x spikes for 60–90 minutes, plus occasional batch-exports overnight.
- Data classification: PHI (highly regulated). SOC 2 Type II compliance required; we will request audit logs and per-request traceability.
- SLA expectations: 99.9% monthly; 200ms p50 target for standard routes.
- Procurement timeline: initial pilot contract 3 months; production rollout Q2 2028.

I've attached the RFP schedule and a rough timeline (attachment: caldera_rfp_schedule.pdf). Can you provide a concise comparison of sizing and operational trade-offs for Private vs Reserved Dedicated so we can include that in the vendor evaluation? We especially care about: procurement lead times, minimum commit sizes, burst strategies, and evidence of auditability for PHI.

Appreciate a short write-up we can circulate with procurement by Thursday.

Best,
Susan Park
Head of Product, Caldera Health

---
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan@calderahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Caldera Health Procurement <procurement@calderahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP: inference hosting for regulated patient workflows

Hi Susan — thanks for the details and the timeline. Quick summary below; I attached a compact capacity model (attachment: capacity_model_v3.xlsx) with selectable inputs so you can tweak QPS and token sizes.

Executive summary (short):
- Private (VPC / private control plane): best for maximum data isolation, full control over network ingress, and simple KMS/HSM integration. Expect longer lead time (4–8 weeks for customer-managed installation; on-prem air-gap longer) and a higher fixed platform fee. Reserved capacity (dedicated pool): faster onboarding (1–2 weeks with Reserved), predictable unit economics, and lower up-front platform cost — but requires contractual commitments for GPU spend and careful tenancy gating for PHI.

Sizing (ballpark for your stated workload):
- Steady-state 35 QPS @ 150 tokens: approximate steady GPU footprint = 4 x A100-80GB equiv (with batching and KV caching configured for interactive latency).
- Peak (3x spike to 105 QPS): burst cushion to handle spikes ~8 GPUs (or autoscale to 12 with short burst credits).
- Overnight batch jobs: add 2–3 lower-priority nodes (can be preemptible) to speed exports without increasing steady committed size.

Key trade-offs:
- Procurement lead time: Private > Reserved (Private requires network + security reviews).
- Commit flexibility: Reserved has minimum monthly commitments; we can structure pilot credits and a staged ramp to reduce initial commitment.
- Auditability: both options provide request-level logs and traceability; Private allows retaining log storage in your VPC which reduces egress concerns.

Next steps:
1) Technical sizing call to validate the QPS profile (30–45 min).
2) If you want, we can provide a formal SOW and a templated security evidence pack (SOC 2 and KMS integration notes).

Would Thursday 10am PST work for a sizing call? Marissa — looping you in for procurement / commercial alignment.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Exec — Healthcare
Redwood Inference

Hi Susan — appreciate the RFP. A couple of commercial notes to help procurement:

- Pilot structure we recommend: 3 months of reserved capacity with ramp credits to limit initial commit risk. We can cap the pilot to a smaller GPU footprint (2 reserved GPUs) and enable burst to cover peak windows.
- SLAs and credits: we can include 99.9% SLA for reserved capacity; Private installs can carry an enterprise SLA and on-call rotation.
- Pricing levers: quantization profiles and batching presets materially change unit cost; we'll include recommended presets in the SOW.

Logan — I'm happy to own the commercial proposal and paperwork once the technical sizing is validated. Susan — is procurement aligned to review a 3-month pilot + conversion clause?

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales — Regulated Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Park <susan@calderahealth.com>, Caldera Health Procurement <procurement@calderahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP: inference hosting for regulated patient workflows

Susan / team — I ran a quick set of microbenchmarks against the model families you mentioned in the RFP and populated a detailed matrix (attachment: redwood_private_dedicated_matrix.pdf). Highlights and recommended configuration: 

- Model: med-tuned opt-6b equivalent. Latency sensitivity: p50 target 200ms requires continuous batching (batch windows tuned to 30–50ms) + KV prefix caching for repeated patient prompts.
- Quantization: int8 quantization with runtime-aware kernels gives ~2.2x token throughput improvement at <1.5% quality delta for summaries. Recommend using the quantized variant for reserved pool to reduce GPU count.

Sizing table (conservative):
- Private (isolated VPC install):
  - Steady-state: 6 x A100-80GB equiv (we recommend extra headroom in private installs because autoscaling is slower).
  - Peak cushion: scale to 12 GPUs via pre-approved burst (requires procurement of burst credits or additional on-prem nodes).
- Reserved Dedicated pool: 
  - Steady-state: 4 x A100-80GB equiv (aggressive batching + int8).
  - Peak cushion: autoscale to 10–12 GPUs using reserved burst lanes; short warm-up of KV cache may add 10–20ms initially.

Operational considerations:
- Cold-start: Private installs with local cache warm-up can take longer to reach p50 targets on sudden spikes; consider pre-warming policies for critical routes.
- Audit logs & retention: we can ship logs to your S3/GCS bucket in Private and to a managed retention store for Reserved. Both provide per-request trace IDs.
- Security: Private supports customer-managed KMS + HSM. Reserved supports envelope encryption and a dedicated key per tenant for PHI separation.
- Cost implications: quantized reserved pool reduces committed GPUs by ~30% vs non-quantized Private baseline. Exact numbers in attached matrix.

I attached the matrix and the paramized capacity model so you can toggle QPS, token size, and quantization to see impacts.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference
